text:
alex: seeing ~30% apiserver 503s in ap-southeast1 starting ~09:12 UTC. controller-manager leader flips a few times, GPU attach failures spike at the same time. looks like a connection/resource exhaustion between proxies and apiserver. rolling alert: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 :grimace:

priya: confirming, I see a short burst of TIME_WAITs in the kube-proxy nodes. nat SNAT table nearing capacity on the edge NAT boxes. GPUs failing attach -> provisioner retries -> retries saturate controlplane.

james: paste of ss from a proxy host a minute ago:
```
$ ss -s
TCP: inuse 1200 orphan 0 tw 820 alloc 1500 mem 2048
TCP: timers 1 (onemore), estab 380, closed 0, orphan 0, synrecv 0, timewait 820
```
looks like tcp_tw is huge. kernel tcp_fin_timeout=60 and tcp_tw_reuse=0 currently.

lia: that explains keepalives not being recycled quickly. controller-manager leader election uses lots of short live connections when watch reconnects. with tw pileup apiserver can't accept new fds -> 503.

sre-oncall: roll up: region egress SNAT exhaustion + host-level TIME_WAIT pile -> apiserver fd pressure -> controller election thrash -> gpu attach retries -> fallback to hosted reserved pool -> temporary cost spike (~$7k over 45m).

alex: can we triage quick mitigation before a bigger rollback? suggestions? :eyes:

priya: immediate mitigation options:
- enable tcp_tw_reuse=1 and lower tcp_fin_timeout to 30 on kube-proxy and NAT hosts (sysctl).
- increase conntrack table size: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max += 100k.
- tune kube-proxy conntrackGC/ttl if available.
- short-term: scale up NAT capacity (add a couple of nats) or route some controlplane egress via fallback region.

james: I'll push a rollout to kube-proxy nodes with `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` and `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30` now to a canary pool. running patch in k8s-tooling: `./scripts/sysctl-apply --nodes canary-proxies tcp_tw_reuse=1 tcp_fin_timeout=30`

deploy-bot: deploy started: sysctl-apply to canary-proxies (5 nodes). ETA 2m.

lia: also recommend increasing apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` and bumping `--max-mutating-requests-inflight` temporarily to relieve rejected requests from heavy retries.

sre-oncall: james, lia, priya — after canary confirms, roll to remaining proxies and NAT hosts. I'll also open a ticket to examine controller-manager watch strategy for high-reconnect patterns (maybe consolidate owners).

james: canary looks good so far, TIME_WAIT down to ~120 on those hosts, apiserver 503s dropped to baseline. rolling to rest of proxies and NATs.

alex: nice. cost team FYI — cost bump due to hosted fallback, PR to billing will follow.

priya: followups: (1) long term: investigate reducing short-lived watch frequency + better connection pooling; (2) autoscale NAT pools by conntrack usage; (3) add alert for apiserver fd pressure and tcp_tw ratio.

lia: filing postmortem draft, assigning owners. will link when ready.

sre-oncall: closing immediate incident; keeping watch for 3h, will reopen if 503s > 5% for 10m. thanks all :thumbsup:
